fact_basis: FY2026 revenue rose 18%, operating income 21%, and Azure Q4 revenue 43%.
Commercial RPO reached USD678B, while standardized capex and FCF were USD115.948B and USD66.987B.
strongest_bear_thesis: AI infrastructure demand is real but economically commoditized; depreciation, leases and model-partner economics absorb the growth before it reaches per-share FCF.
hidden_assumptions: Azure demand is incremental rather than pulled forward.
Copilot price and usage offset seat and workflow cannibalization.
AI gross profit grows faster than the fixed-capital base.
falsifiers: Two consecutive periods of falling Azure growth and cloud gross margin despite rising AI capex.
Per-share FCF remains below FY2025 after normalizing leases and one-off gains through FY2028.
Paid Copilot seats or revenue retention stall while inference usage rises.
underweighted_evidence: The Anthropic gain inflated reported earnings.
The capex-to-FCF gap and partner commitments reduce downside flexibility.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Sustained low-teens revenue growth with mid-20s terminal FCF margin.
permanent_loss_event: AI capacity is stranded while cloud pricing power weakens and contractual commitments remain fixed.
inference: The platform thesis survives, but the cash-return mechanism is not yet proven.
opinion: Keep WATCH and rewrite the thesis around per-share AI cash returns, not Azure demand alone.

fact_basis: Q2 revenue rose 20%, operating income 43%, AWS 37%, and advertising 26%.
Standardized capex was USD173.028B and TTM FCF was negative USD11.625B; the Anthropic gain is excluded from operating economics.
strongest_bear_thesis: AWS, retail and advertising growth conceal a permanent rise in capital intensity, leaving shareholders with weak cash conversion despite multiple strong revenue engines.
hidden_assumptions: AWS AI capacity reaches high utilization before pricing falls.
Retail logistics retains margin gains through a recession.
Advertising growth remains independent of marketplace subsidy and traffic costs.
falsifiers: AWS operating profit grows slower than depreciation and lease-adjusted invested capital for four quarters.
Retail contribution margins reverse while fulfillment capex stays elevated.
Normalized FCF remains negative after excluding investment gains through 2028.
underweighted_evidence: Lease and purchase commitments are less flexible than reported capex.
A large non-operating gain can obscure weak cash conversion.
valuation_dominant_assumption: A durable double-digit growth blend with FCF margin approaching 9-12%.
permanent_loss_event: AI leases and logistics fixed costs remain while AWS pricing and retail volumes normalize together.
inference: The diversified moat remains credible, but base-case returns do not clear the hurdle.
opinion: Keep WATCH and require segment-level incremental ROIC before promotion.

fact_basis: Q2 revenue rose 28%, ad impressions 14%, and price per ad 12%.
Quarterly FCF fell to USD0.784B and 2026 capex guidance reached USD130-145B while Reality Labs continued to lose money.
strongest_bear_thesis: The ad network funds two open-ended capital programs—frontier AI infrastructure and Reality Labs—whose returns may arrive after attention and regulatory advantages weaken.
hidden_assumptions: Recommendation AI creates incremental monetization rather than temporary engagement lift.
Open-model strategy does not commoditize Meta's infrastructure spend.
Management will curtail low-return projects before core cash flow is impaired.
falsifiers: Ad price or conversion weakens for two periods despite rising compute.
Reality Labs plus AI capex consumes more than half of core operating cash flow through 2028.
Daily-user growth or time spent shifts structurally toward competing generative interfaces.
underweighted_evidence: Debt rose while capital intensity accelerated.
The apparent moat improvement is partly contemporaneous revenue growth, not yet switching-cost evidence.
valuation_dominant_assumption: AI sustains high-single-digit growth and restores mid-20s FCF margins.
permanent_loss_event: Core attention erodes before the combined AI and metaverse asset base earns its cost of capital.
inference: The advertising moat is strong, but capital-allocation discipline is the controlling uncertainty.
opinion: Keep WATCH and cap the valuation until combined program cash returns are observable.

fact_basis: The reverse model haircuts the starting FCF margin to 20% for SBC and still produces a 12.9% base IRR.
Reported growth and enterprise workflow breadth support cross-sell, but reported cash margin is materially above the economic estimate.
strongest_bear_thesis: Autonomous agents bypass the workflow layer, turning ServiceNow from a control plane into an expensive system of record while SBC continues to transfer value from owners.
hidden_assumptions: Enterprises keep ServiceNow as the orchestration layer for third-party agents.
AI monetization exceeds inference and acquisition costs.
SBC-adjusted FCF margins expand without weakening retention.
falsifiers: Renewal rate or net expansion declines alongside AI-agent adoption for two consecutive periods.
SBC-adjusted per-share FCF grows below revenue for six quarters.
Large customers shift material workflows to cloud-vendor-native agent platforms.
underweighted_evidence: The economic 20% starting FCF margin is far below the headline cash margin.
Platform acquisitions can mask organic product productivity.
valuation_dominant_assumption: ServiceNow remains the enterprise workflow control plane and sustains mid-teens growth.
permanent_loss_event: AI disintermediation coincides with persistent dilution and multiple compression.
inference: The bear case is material, but the valuation gap survives a conservative SBC adjustment.
opinion: Red-team PASS means the thesis survives this attack; keep WATCH until moat and dilution falsifiers are tested.

fact_basis: An aggressive bull with 26% revenue CAGR, 32% terminal FCF margin, and 30x terminal P/FCF returns only 10.1% over ten years.
Diluted shares increased about 4.5% year over year and operational-integrity questions remain after a major service disruption.
strongest_bear_thesis: A premium security platform suffers trust loss and ongoing dilution just as growth normalizes, causing both cash expectations and the extreme terminal multiple to contract.
hidden_assumptions: Platform consolidation permanently offsets module-level competition.
SBC dilution falls rapidly while talent retention remains intact.
The market will still award 30x FCF after a decade of maturation.
falsifiers: The bull case fails to exceed the 9% hurdle after realistic dilution.
Net retention or new-logo growth weakens while sales efficiency fails to recover.
Operational remediation does not prevent another material customer-impacting outage.
underweighted_evidence: The valuation already capitalizes exceptional execution.
Reported cash flow treats SBC as non-cash despite recurring owner dilution.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Bull-plus duration and a 30x terminal multiple.
permanent_loss_event: Trust impairment, competition, and dilution converge during multiple normalization.
inference: Business quality cannot offset the absence of a defensible expectation gap.
opinion: Retain the price Hard Veto and SCREEN_OUT.

fact_basis: Q2 revenue rose 48%; volume rose 60% while realized price fell 13%, led by Mounjaro and Zepbound.
The company expanded manufacturing and completed multiple acquisitions while the modeled base IRR was 3.3%.
strongest_bear_thesis: Tirzepatide volume masks deteriorating price and access economics while manufacturing and acquisition commitments peak ahead of competition and concentration normalization.
hidden_assumptions: Long-duration adherence and reimbursement support current volume economics.
Next-generation obesity assets extend rather than cannibalize the franchise.
Manufacturing and acquired R&D earn returns above the cost of capital.
falsifiers: Net realized price and persistence decline faster than manufacturing unit cost.
Cardiometabolic concentration remains dominant as competitive capacity expands.
Acquired programs fail while capex-to-sales remains elevated.
underweighted_evidence: The 13% price decline matters more than headline 60% volume growth.
IPR&D cash outlays are economic reinvestment, not one-off noise.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Mid-teens decade growth and durable premium margins across the obesity franchise.
permanent_loss_event: Access pressure and competition hit the concentrated franchise before fixed manufacturing and acquisition capital is recovered.
inference: The scientific platform is strong, but current price leaves the base case below the hurdle.
opinion: Keep WATCH and use a product-level access and return model before promotion.

fact_basis: Q2 revenue rose 12%; JOURNAVX and CASGEVY began contributing but remained small relative to cystic-fibrosis cash flow.
The announced Crinetics acquisition costs about USD8.8B net of target cash; modeled base IRR was 1.9% and bull 13.3%.
strongest_bear_thesis: The CF franchise matures before non-CF launches and the large Crinetics acquisition replace its cash flow, converting balance-sheet strength into pipeline concentration risk.
hidden_assumptions: CF pricing and patent duration remain resilient.
JOURNAVX and CASGEVY overcome reimbursement and delivery friction.
Crinetics assets justify the acquisition price after clinical failure risk.
falsifiers: CF patient growth and net price weaken before non-CF revenue exceeds the stated threshold.
CASGEVY treatment-center throughput or reimbursement stalls.
Crinetics milestones slip or pivotal data reduce risk-adjusted value.
underweighted_evidence: The base valuation does not clear the hurdle.
Gene-therapy delivery complexity limits TAM-to-cash conversion.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Timely diversification before CF duration fades.
permanent_loss_event: CF erosion and non-CF clinical or commercial failure coincide after the cash-funded acquisition.
inference: Pipeline optionality is real, but the price requires successful diversification.
opinion: Keep WATCH and revise the thesis into product-level probabilities.

fact_basis: Q2 ARR rose 39% and net revenue retention was 126%.
H1 SBC of USD278.7M exceeded GAAP net income of USD198.7M; the company also issued shares through an ATM, and future bookings include cancellable provisions.
strongest_bear_thesis: A strong public-safety platform overstates per-share economics through SBC, acquisition shares, ATM issuance and bookings that are less firm than backlog language implies.
hidden_assumptions: Bookings convert at historic rates despite cancellation and budget clauses.
SBC falls as a share of revenue without raising cash compensation.
AI and drone expansion strengthen rather than complicate contract economics.
falsifiers: Diluted share growth remains above per-share FCF growth.
RPO conversion weakens or public budgets delay deployments.
Remediated revenue controls recur or generate restatements.
underweighted_evidence: SBC exceeded GAAP net income.
The internal-control history raises confidence requirements even after remediation.
valuation_dominant_assumption: High-teens growth with large software margin expansion and controlled dilution.
permanent_loss_event: Contract-quality disappointment and control failure meet persistent dilution at a premium multiple.
inference: Customer value is strong, but reported growth is not equivalent to owner return.
opinion: Keep WATCH and require a fully diluted, non-cancellable contract model.

fact_basis: Q2 organic sales grew 14% with broad electrical and aerospace orders.
Eaton paid about USD9.549B net for Boyd Thermal, with preliminary intangible assets and goodwill exceeding the purchase price before other adjustments; modeled bull IRR was 10.6%.
strongest_bear_thesis: Late-cycle electrification strength and a richly priced thermal acquisition inflate reported growth just before order and margin normalization.
hidden_assumptions: Data-center and grid orders represent final demand rather than double ordering.
Boyd synergies offset the high intangible purchase price.
Mobility separation does not distract operations or remove cash support.
falsifiers: Organic orders turn negative as capacity comes online.
Boyd's incremental operating profit fails to cover a reasonable capital charge.
Electrical margins revert while working capital and capex remain elevated.
underweighted_evidence: Acquisition contribution was already 7% of quarterly growth.
The bull case barely clears the hurdle.
valuation_dominant_assumption: A long electrical upcycle plus successful Boyd integration.
permanent_loss_event: Order normalization and acquisition impairment occur together.
inference: Structural demand exists, but much of it is priced and capital allocation raises downside.
opinion: Keep WATCH and isolate organic ROIC before promotion.

fact_basis: Q2 organic revenue rose 18% and adjusted operating margin reached 22.6%.
Prior organic orders rose 252%, book-to-bill was about 2.9x, and backlog reached USD15B; the modeled bull IRR was 11.2%.
strongest_bear_thesis: AI infrastructure scarcity creates peak orders, advances and margins that reverse when hyperscalers digest capacity and competitors expand supply.
hidden_assumptions: Backlog is non-cancellable and free of double ordering.
Current price and margin persist after supply bottlenecks clear.
Customer concentration does not increase bargaining power against Vertiv.
falsifiers: Cancellations or schedule slips rise while book-to-bill falls below one.
Advance-driven cash flow reverses into working-capital outflow.
Organic growth falls below capacity additions and adjusted margin contracts.
underweighted_evidence: Order growth far exceeds end-market deployment growth.
The current price sits near an aggressive bull even after cash-flow normalization.
valuation_dominant_assumption: A decade-long AI power and cooling supercycle with high-teens margins.
permanent_loss_event: Hyperscaler digestion, cancellations and capacity overbuild hit simultaneously.
inference: The bottleneck is real, but cycle duration and order quality remain unproven.
opinion: Keep WATCH with price and concentration gates open.

fact_basis: FY2025 revenue and operating profit were KRW97.147T and KRW47.206T; preliminary Q2 2026 revenue and operating profit were KRW79.319T and KRW60.543T.
Official Q2 cash and debt imply about KRW69.4T net cash; the cycle model's bull IRR is 10.5%.
strongest_bear_thesis: HBM scarcity and a preliminary peak-profit quarter are capitalized as durable economics while memory capacity, customer bargaining power and enormous capex restore cyclicality before cash conversion catches up.
hidden_assumptions: HBM technology leadership persists across customer qualification cycles.
The 2026 profit step-up converts into FCF after capex and working capital.
A cyclical memory producer retains a 15x terminal FCF multiple.
falsifiers: HBM share, yield or gross margin declines at two major customers.
Audited FCF remains far below operating profit while capex expands.
Supply additions cause pricing and utilization to normalize faster than modeled.
underweighted_evidence: Q2 figures are preliminary and unusually far above FY2025 quarterly economics.
Long-term agreements reduce volume risk but can shift price and capacity risk.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Sustained triple-digit-trillion won FCF and a structurally higher terminal multiple.
permanent_loss_event: Technology-share loss and memory oversupply coincide with peak capacity investment.
inference: The balance-sheet anomaly is resolved, but price and cycle risk are not.
opinion: Score the model at one of six and retain WATCH under a price/cycle INVESTIGATE gate.

fact_basis: Revenue and capacity growth remain strong, but the reverse model's base IRR was 2.9% and bull 11.1%.
New-plant utilization, acquisition funding and customer concentration remain the main open evidence gates.
strongest_bear_thesis: Biologics outsourcing growth is real, yet current value assumes near-continuous utilization of new capacity and successful acquisition integration despite concentrated customers and long validation cycles.
hidden_assumptions: Plants ramp near plan without pricing concessions.
Customer molecules succeed and remain with the platform.
Acquisition and expansion capital earn historical returns.
falsifiers: Plant utilization or signed backlog conversion falls below plan.
Top-customer concentration rises while price per batch declines.
Post-acquisition ROIC remains below the hurdle after a full ramp cycle.
underweighted_evidence: Capacity is not demand until validated batches convert to cash.
The bull only narrowly clears the Korean hurdle.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Sustained high-teens growth with low-20s FCF margins and high utilization.
permanent_loss_event: Customer program failures and plant underutilization coincide after fixed-cost expansion.
inference: The moat can widen through scale, but the price already recognizes much of the build-out.
opinion: Keep WATCH and require plant-level returns and customer concentration evidence.

fact_basis: FY2025 owner-attributable profit was KRW9.446T; Q2 2026 revenue, operating profit and net profit were KRW49.215T, KRW2.851T and KRW2.888T.
Q2 volume fell 6.9%; 2026 guidance calls for 1-2% revenue growth and a 6.3-7.3% operating margin.
strongest_bear_thesis: A low earnings multiple is a value trap if auto incentives, tariffs and EV investment compress manufacturing returns while captive-finance credit losses rise into the same downturn.
hidden_assumptions: Hybrid mix offsets weaker unit volume and incentives.
US and EV capacity earns returns above the cost of capital.
Finance earnings and funding remain resilient through a credit cycle.
falsifiers: Auto margin falls below guidance while inventories and incentives rise.
Finance delinquencies and loss provisions outgrow receivables.
Owner earnings fail to compound at the roughly 8% reverse requirement.
underweighted_evidence: Consolidated debt is mainly operating finance funding but still creates correlated downside.
Preferred-share and class-specific rights make simple common-share valuation misleading.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Near-8% owner-earnings growth or a favorable exit multiple despite mature auto demand.
permanent_loss_event: Manufacturing margin and captive-finance credit deteriorate simultaneously during an investment peak.
inference: The price is not a veto, but the base owner-earnings case does not clear 10%.
opinion: Assign two of six, retain WATCH, and make segment capital returns the next gate.

fact_basis: Defense backlog and export programs provide multi-year visibility.
A June 2026 factory explosion and fire killed five people; prior capital raising and customer or country concentration remain open.
strongest_bear_thesis: Headline backlog masks safety, execution, sovereign-customer and working-capital risks while prior dilution shows that growth can be financed at shareholders' expense.
hidden_assumptions: Backlog converts without cancellations, penalties or geopolitical restrictions.
Safety remediation prevents operational recurrence.
Advance payments and capex produce high per-share returns after dilution.
falsifiers: Another material safety event or regulator finding occurs.
Export milestones slip and contract assets or receivables rise faster than sales.
Diluted per-share FCF lags operating profit through the delivery cycle.
underweighted_evidence: Fatal safety outcomes are an operational-integrity signal, not merely an ESG footnote.
Contract advances can temporarily flatter cash conversion.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Durable export backlog conversion with expanding margins.
permanent_loss_event: Safety failure and delivery penalties trigger contract loss and further dilution.
inference: Structural defense demand does not neutralize execution and integrity risk.
opinion: Keep WATCH; do not promote before independent safety and contract-quality evidence.

fact_basis: Grid and data-center demand support current growth, but standardized FCF is weak after capex and working capital.
The model requires 19.7% ten-year revenue growth at a 10% terminal FCF margin; base IRR was negative 1.1% and bull 11.4%.
strongest_bear_thesis: North American electrical scarcity is extrapolated into a decade of growth while expansion and working capital consume cash and competitive capacity catches up.
hidden_assumptions: Current orders are final demand rather than channel or project pull-forward.
FCF margins rise despite working-capital intensity.
North American growth offsets domestic and product concentration.
falsifiers: Book-to-bill normalizes before new capacity reaches target utilization.
Receivables and inventory continue to outgrow sales.
FCF margin remains below the modeled path as capex matures.
underweighted_evidence: Reported earnings growth has not yet translated into comparable free cash flow.
The bull barely clears the hurdle.
valuation_dominant_assumption: A long high-growth period plus material FCF-margin expansion.
permanent_loss_event: Demand normalization leaves excess capacity and trapped working capital.
inference: The theme is structural, but the security price embeds too much of it.
opinion: Keep WATCH under price and incremental-ROIC gates.

fact_basis: Q2 revenue rose 26%, operating profit 37.3%, and operating margin reached 25.1%.
Order backlog was KRW12.31T and exports were 78% of H1 sales; base IRR was negative 0.8% and bull 11.9%.
strongest_bear_thesis: Transformer shortages create peak pricing, backlog and 25% margins that all normalize as global capacity expands, while the current price treats the supercycle as structural permanence.
hidden_assumptions: Backlog is firm and reprices favorably.
North American shortage economics persist after competitor expansion.
New capacity is filled without sacrificing margin.
falsifiers: Backlog cancellations or lead-time compression accelerate.
Price or mix contribution turns negative for two periods.
Capacity additions outpace order growth and working capital reverses.
underweighted_evidence: The margin is far above historical cycle economics.
Export and product concentration amplify a common shock.
valuation_dominant_assumption: High-teens decade growth with sustained mid-teens FCF margins.
permanent_loss_event: Supply normalization causes simultaneous price, margin and multiple compression.
inference: A real bottleneck is being priced as a durable moat.
opinion: Keep WATCH; require normalized-cycle returns before promotion.

fact_basis: Q2 revenue rose 16.2% while operating profit fell 0.2% under AI investment.
The model includes the announced NVIDIA placement through at least 159.28M pro-forma shares; base IRR is 12.0%.
strongest_bear_thesis: Generative interfaces weaken search entry-point power while AI data-center and overseas C2C investments consume the cash that makes the apparent valuation gap attractive.
hidden_assumptions: Search and commerce data remain proprietary enough to defend user intent.
AI investment improves monetization faster than depreciation rises.
No further material dilution is needed to fund infrastructure.
falsifiers: Search share, query growth or ad conversion declines for two periods.
AI-related capex grows while operating profit and per-share FCF remain flat.
Further strategic issuance pushes dilution materially above the modeled floor.
underweighted_evidence: Revenue growth did not translate into operating-profit growth.
The favorable model depends on FCF-margin recovery after heavy infrastructure spend.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Search moat persists and AI investment restores high-teens FCF margins.
permanent_loss_event: Search traffic migrates while fixed AI assets and dilution remain.
inference: The gap survives known dilution and a conservative bear, so the thesis survives this red-team round.
opinion: PASS the thesis, not the stock; retain WATCH until search and per-share cash falsifiers clear.

fact_basis: Q2 revenue rose 94.9% and operating profit 67%; Subnautica 2 sold five million units in 22 days.

The Delaware Court of Chancery entered judgment that Krafton breached the acquisition agreement by terminating key employees without valid cause and improperly seizing operational control; the parties later settled on undisclosed financial terms.
strongest_bear_thesis: Strong game economics are paired with a court-documented willingness by senior management to override a negotiated earn-out and studio control, impairing trust in acquisition discipline and talent retention.
hidden_assumptions: The conduct was isolated rather than representative of capital-allocation culture.
The confidential settlement fully caps financial and reputational costs.
Acquired creative teams will still trust Krafton's autonomy commitments.
falsifiers: The primary falsifier has already triggered: a final court judgment found contractual breach and improper seizure of control.
Independent governance remediation and quantified settlement economics would be required to reconsider.
Future acquisitions must show durable founder retention and contract compliance.
underweighted_evidence: The earlier thesis treated the matter as a generic dispute; the court's findings are materially stronger evidence.
Subnautica 2's commercial success can distract from the governance mechanism that created the risk.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Low implied growth and strong current FCF, neither of which repairs management-integrity impairment.
permanent_loss_event: Repeated acquisition-governance conduct drives talent loss, litigation and destruction of acquired IP value.
inference: The settlement closes litigation but does not erase the adjudicated conduct.
opinion: Set management_or_accounting_integrity to FAIL; Hard Veto overrides the 40-point B score.

fact_basis: H1 revenue was KRW140.493B and operating profit KRW73.481B.

Multiple partner contracts and Qlex sales validate ALT-B4, but most milestones and royalties are contingent or confidential; the probability-tree bull IRR is 11.1% while probability-weighted IRR is approximately zero.
strongest_bear_thesis: Investors capitalize undiscounted milestone headlines and low-single-digit royalties as certain while partner clinical failure, IP/FTO, timing and manufacturing risks leave most cash flows binary.
hidden_assumptions: Qlex conversion reaches broad Keytruda-family adoption.
Multiple partner assets win approval without IP restrictions.
Royalty and supply economics are large enough despite confidential terms.
falsifiers: Qlex sales growth or conversion stalls before milestone thresholds.
A partner program fails, is deprioritized, or encounters material FTO litigation.
Facility spending rises without contracted supply volume and cash milestones.
underweighted_evidence: Contract maxima are not probability-weighted revenue.
The low-single-digit Merck royalty begins only after all sales milestones are achieved.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Several independent partner successes, not merely Keytruda Qlex approval.
permanent_loss_event: Partner or IP failures remove contingent cash while the new fixed-cost facility remains.
inference: Platform validation is real, but the current price requires the narrow multi-success branch.
opinion: Assign one of six and retain WATCH under contract, IP and price gates.

fact_basis: Revenue growth and overseas expansion are exceptionally strong, with overseas sales around 92% of the mix.
The model's base IRR was 2.9% and bull 14.4%; repurchase cohorts, CAC, sell-through and inventory durability remain unverified.
strongest_bear_thesis: Viral hero-product and platform-channel growth is mistaken for a durable brand moat, leaving inventory, returns and acquisition costs exposed when social attention shifts.
hidden_assumptions: Device and skincare cohorts repurchase at durable rates.
Overseas channel sell-through matches shipments.
CAC stays low as the brand expands beyond hero products.
falsifiers: Repeat purchase or cohort revenue declines as paid acquisition rises.
Channel inventory and returns outgrow end demand.
New-product contribution fails to reduce hero-SKU concentration.
underweighted_evidence: Overseas concentration converts one global trend reversal into a company-wide shock.
Headline revenue does not independently prove customer lifetime value.
valuation_dominant_assumption: Long global brand duration with high-teens FCF margins.
permanent_loss_event: Social demand reverses while channel inventory and CAC spike together.
inference: The growth is genuine, but moat and unit economics remain unproven at the current price.
opinion: Keep WATCH and require cohort and sell-through data before promotion.
